problems.description: 33 naming-convention violations across new files (functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE, classes/interfaces not PascalCase), driving convention score to 0.50; the replaced seed followed these conventions, so this is a regression.
Cognitive complexity increased by +29 across the new generator/cli/dev-server code.
index.ts seed replaced wholesale (200→2 lines, full rewrite into a different application domain) rather than built upon; acceptable for greenfield Session 1, but discards the existing structure.

strengths: Thin barrel entry (index.ts re-exports from src/generator) with clean separation of generator logic and CLI arg parsing
Proper TypeScript tooling: jest + ts-jest config, package.json with bin/main/scripts, minimal dependency set
Measured improvements: 0 new bugs, -3 code smells, 0% duplication, and tests added
Tests directory wired into testMatch with a runnable npm test script
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent greenfield module layout with good tooling and reduced smells, but dragged down by 33 naming-convention violations (0.50 score) and +29 cognitive complexity versus the clean seed it replaced.

problems.description: BuildOptions adds both `templatesDir` and a redundant `templateDir` alias in generator.ts; the plumbing in cli.ts and buildSite() only uses `templatesDir`, so the extra field is dead surface area.

Page gains an open `[key: string]: unknown` index signature in generator.ts, which loosens type safety across the whole page model rather than declaring only the two new frontmatter fields (template, layout).

Measured convention score is 0.50 (33 violations), but every listed violation is in index.ts and dev-server.ts — files NOT touched by this diff. The convention_adherence score of 0.70 reflects this commit's own files (all camelCase/PascalCase per convention); the 0.50 appears to be pre-existing baseline debt, not introduced here.
Adds `handlebars` ^4.7.8 dependency; justified by the feature, but no README/docs mention the new templates/partials convention.

strengths: Templating is cleanly factored into small single-purpose functions (templateFile, createRenderer, renderWithLayout, renderPage, renderIndex) with a graceful fallback to the existing document() output when no templates exist.
Feature is backward compatible: existing build paths keep working when templatesDir is absent.
Mechanical measurements support a good change: 0 new bugs, 0 duplications, and cognitive complexity improved by -27 despite +99 lines.
Touched files follow existing naming and style conventions; test coverage was extended alongside the feature.
Partial registration is scoped to an isolated Handlebars instance (Handlebars.create()), avoiding global registry pollution.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, backward-compatible templating feature with good factoring and lower cognitive complexity that introduces only minor debt (a redundant templateDir alias and a loosened Page index signature), while the low 0.50 convention score stems from pre-existing violations in untouched files.

problems.description: No tests added for server.ts despite jest/ts-jest being configured; the dev server (http handling, websocket reload, chokidar rebuild, path-traversal guard) is entirely untested.
cli.ts parses args twice on the build path (once into `options`, again via `parseArgs(args)`) and the second call is unnecessary.

Measured convention score is 0.50 (33 violations), but the listed violations reference index.ts declarations and a 'dev-server.ts' file that don't exist in this diff — the violation report appears misattributed.
Each request does three synchronous syscalls (existsSync, statSync, readFileSync) and a full buildSite run on server start blocks the listen callback.

strengths: Reuses buildSite and extends the existing BuildOptions type via ServeOptions instead of duplicating build logic.
Path-traversal guard using path.resolve + prefix check before serving files.
Clean shutdown path in close() that clears the debounce timer, closes watcher and websocket clients, and awaits server close.
Debounced rebuilds (50ms) prevent rebuild storms, and CLI wiring/package.json/index.ts exports are updated consistently.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated feature that fits the existing architecture and reuses core types, but the measured 0.50 convention score does not match the actual diff (the reported violations reference a nonexistent 'dev-server.ts' and declarations index.ts doesn't define) and it ships without any test coverage.

problems.description: DevServerPlugin.close() is a single dense async line mixing watcher teardown, socket terminate, and server close; dev-server.ts packs reloadScript/injectReloadScript/contentType as one-liners, consistent with the +25 cognitive complexity delta

MarkdownPlugin casts Page to `Page & { source: string }` in three places, suggesting the Page type was not extended to model its own source path; a typed field or a plugin context change would avoid the cast

Mechanical convention score is 0.50 with 33 reported violations (Functions should use camelCase, Classes/Interfaces PascalCase, Constants UPPER_CASE) across index.ts and dev-server.ts; the listed examples look like false positives from a tool that does not recognize const arrow functions or default exports, so qualitative judgment disagrees with the measurement
Refactor touches WebSocket upgrade handling, chokidar watching, and path-traversal guarding with no tests visible in the diff

strengths: Net -195/+220 line refactor that extracts dev-server, markdown, and template concerns into a coherent Plugin interface with BuildContext and SSGConfig
Re-exports plugins through index.ts, matching the existing barrel export pattern (BuildOptions, Page, DevServer, ServeOptions)
Path-traversal guard in static serving returns 403 before resolving output paths
Debounced rebuilds with WebSocket-based reload and explicit error handling in async paths
Consistent option naming (contentDir/templatesDir/outputDir) reused from the existing BuildOptions surface
commit_reviews.summary: A clean plugin-extraction refactor that reduces line count and centralizes server/markdown/template concerns, though it scores 0.50 on the mechanical convention check due to apparent analyzer false positives on const arrow functions and default exports.

problems.description: Date handling changed from deterministic `date.toISOString()` to `String(parsed.data.date)`, which is locale/timezone-dependent for Date values — silently changes rendered output for existing content.

Markdown and template plugins share one mutable `context.cache.pages` map where the markdown plugin seeds partially-populated entries (`output: cached?.output ?? ''`, `templateHash` not its own) that the template plugin later fills — cross-plugin coupling that breaks if a third plugin touches the cache.

Incremental caching adds subtle invalidation paths (+4 functions, +144 lines) with zero tests added; cache-hit/skip logic (sourceHash/templateHash/output/existsSync) is exactly where regressions hide.
`--clean` is parsed in cli.ts but no consumption of `options.clean` is visible in the generator diff — potentially a dead option that users will expect to clear the cache manifest.
Internal `_sourceHash`/`_sourceRelative` fields leak onto the exported public `Page` type, polluting the plugin-facing contract with implementation detail.
Measured +13 cognitive complexity / +4 smells track the lazy-parse IIFE and nested cache-check conditional in template.ts — dense logic that would benefit from extraction.

strengths: Coherent cross-cutting feature spanning CLI flags, generator, and both plugins with a single BuildOptions extension point.
Cache invalidation uses SHA256 source hashing via stdlib `node:crypto` — no new dependencies.
Typed `BuildStats`/`CachePage`/`BuildManifest` exports and a clean `getLastBuildStats()` API wired into CLI output.
Cache keyed by relative path and shared across plugins keeps one source of truth for build state.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-architected incremental-build feature that fits the existing plugin/BuildContext model and is net-better, but the measured 0.50 convention score reflects pre-existing whole-file lint issues (dev-server.ts is untouched by this diff) rather than this commit's camelCase/PascalCase-clean additions — while the +13 cognitive complexity, cross-plugin cache coupling, and date-format behavior change justify the technical-debt flag.

compounding_issues: Session 4's plugin refactor broke the build and test suite (TS2339 union-type errors on optional Plugin hooks; DevServerPlugin not structurally compatible with Plugin), and session 5 never repaired it — the final commit does not compile and zero tests pass
Session 5 added a syntax error in src/cli.ts (stray closing brace on line 25, TS1128) on top of the session 4 breakage, shipping a non-running binary
Verification environment failures compounded damage: later sessions' jest/npm calls returned 'command not found', so the S4/S5 regressions went unnoticed
Plugin API inconsistency: concrete plugins (MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin) only implement onFile while generator calls onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onEnd on a union type that lacks them
Config surface drift: templatesDir/templateDir aliasing plus --incremental/--clean flags layered onto an already-broken parse loop
key_decisions: S1 greenfield: replace the seed auth API with a self-contained static site generator (gray-matter + marked, recursive markdown discovery, built-in document() fallback)
S2 feature: adopt Handlebars with partials/layouts and frontmatter-driven per-page template selection while preserving default output
S3 integration: add ssg serve with chokidar watch + WebSocket live-reload and path-traversal guards
S4 refactor: extract a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (plugins/ dir, Plugin interface, generator pipeline) — the most consequential choice, and the one that destabilized the codebase
S5 cross-cutting: incremental builds via SHA-256 content/template hashing + .ssg-cache.json manifest + build stats (pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped/timeSaved)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily through sessions 1-3: each session compiled cleanly, tests grew from 2 to 4 passing, and the feature layering (core generator -> templating -> dev server) was coherent. Session 4's plugin refactor was architecturally ambitious but regressed the codebase — TypeScript type errors broke compilation and the test suite went from 4 passing to 0. Session 5 added a genuinely useful incremental-caching feature but stacked a syntax error on top of the un-repaired refactor, leaving the final commit non-compiling with no passing tests. The narrative arc was logical; the engineering arc collapsed in the final two sessions.
story_review.summary: A coherent feature-addition narrative whose last two sessions shipped a broken build and zero passing tests, undercutting a strong greenfield-through-integration start.
